commercial_incentive: explicitly promotes his own paid one-on-one consulting and a 'parents ultimate course on college admissions' at the end
key_insights: Defines reach schools as those where the student's academic profile falls on the lower end of the school's admitted range, noting virtually all 'highly selective/highly rejective' colleges are reach schools for nearly everyone.
Defines match/target schools as roughly corresponding to an admit-rate range of about 25-50%, where the student's profile aligns closely with the school's average admitted student.

Defines likely schools as those where the student's profile exceeds the average, noting community colleges and schools admitting more than 75% of applicants are essentially automatic likely schools for virtually everyone.
Warns families to compare their stats against published admitted-student data specifically, not enrolled-student data, since admitted-student stats run higher.

Breaks 'fit' into three dimensions beyond academics: academic fit (class size, research-institution vs. small-school environment), social fit (campus culture, size, politics), and financial fit (recommends using each college's net price calculator rather than the sticker price).
Cites a national average of about 7 college applications per student, but recommends most students target 8-10 schools (roughly 1-2 likely, 3-4 match, 3-4 reach).

Recommends high-financial-need families widen their list to around 15 schools, and international students needing aid widen to 15-20+, citing roughly 1-2% admit rates for internationally-aided applicants at the most selective, need-blind-limited schools.
Outlines a four-step narrowing process: research broadly (30-40 schools), identify family non-negotiables, discuss and reflect as a family, then finalize the list.
specific_numbers_or_facts: National average application count cited as about 7 schools per student (stated by presenter)
Recommended list size: 8-10 schools total for most students (stated by presenter)
Match/target schools associated with roughly 25-50% admit rates; likely schools associated with >75% admit rates (stated by presenter)

High-financial-need families advised to widen to about 15 schools; international students needing aid advised toward 15-20+ schools, with admit rates cited around 1-2% for that group (stated by presenter)
notable_or_distinctive: Unusually specific in tying 'match' and 'likely' labels to numeric admit-rate bands, and in giving differentiated list-size recommendations by financial-need and international status rather than one blanket number.
reliability_notes: The 'national average of 7 applications' and the admit-rate band figures are stated without citation in the transcript; video ends with a pitch for the presenter's own paid consulting and course.
